# 193 · A bulk order's quote event dropped in the refactor, refuted on the route's trace of sends

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✗ Violation: counterexample found** | functional | high | refactor, behaviour change not intended | [`QuotesController#quote`](../../examples/apps/shop/src/main/java/shop/QuotesController.java) | [B9: Regression verification](../../lib/README.md) |

> The value-object refactor of 190, with the route sending no `QuoteEvent` for an order of 100 items or more. The total is the same on every request, so every test of the answer passes. The tool compares the ordered trace of the route's sends and refutes it on a 100-item order, the witness replayed on the JVM under recording stubs.

Tags: [payments](../README.md#tag-payments), [spring-boot](../README.md#tag-spring-boot), [messaging](../README.md#tag-messaging), [dropped-case](../README.md#tag-dropped-case), [joint-run](../README.md#tag-joint-run), [effect-trace](../README.md#tag-effect-trace), [own-checker](../README.md#tag-own-checker)

## The change

`Quote`'s amount, a `long` of cents, becomes a value object, `Money`, so `Quote(long cents, int quantity)` is now `Quote(Money amount, int quantity)`; `Pricing.total` reads `q.amount.cents()` where it read `q.cents`; the pure helper `Pricing.discount` (a tenth off ten items or more) is rewritten as an early return; and the route `POST /quotes` makes the quote with `new Money(cents)`. Nothing is meant to change: not the total, not the event the route sends, not what `Pricing.withQuantity` hands back. In this version the route also sends the event only when `quantity < 100`.

**Before** ([`QuotesController.java`](../../examples/apps/shop/src/main/java/shop/QuotesController.java), line 16):

```java

    @PostMapping("/quotes")
    public long quote(@RequestParam long cents, @RequestParam int quantity) {
        long total = Pricing.total(new Quote(cents, quantity));
        if (total > 0) kafka.send("quotes", new QuoteEvent(total, quantity));
        return total;
    }

    /** The case this loop leaves unresolved: a string response, built by string concatenation. */
    @PostMapping("/quotes/text")
    public String quoteText(@RequestParam long cents, @RequestParam int quantity) {
        return "total " + Pricing.total(new Quote(cents, quantity));
    }
}
```

**After:**

```java

    @PostMapping("/quotes")
    public long quote(@RequestParam long cents, @RequestParam int quantity) {
        long total = Pricing.total(new Quote(new Money(cents), quantity));
        if (total > 0 && quantity < 100) kafka.send("quotes", new QuoteEvent(total, quantity));
        return total;
    }

    /** The case this loop leaves unresolved: a string response, built by string concatenation. */
    @PostMapping("/quotes/text")
    public String quoteText(@RequestParam long cents, @RequestParam int quantity) {
        return "total " + Pricing.total(new Quote(new Money(cents), quantity));
    }
}
```

## What the verifier found

The two builds disagree on `shop.QuotesController#quote`. The checker found this input, and the verifier replayed it on the JVM against both builds (an entry point under the same recording stubs, a kernel method with its objects made by their constructors):

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /quotes: cents=1, quantity=100` | `returns 90; KafkaTemplate.send(topic="quotes", data.total=90, data.quantity=100)` | `returns 90; no modeled call` |

The domain is `cents: long × quantity: int (the request's inputs, the same in both builds)`.

Every part the run checked, nothing written by hand (the entry points under their observation specs, each kernel pair under the correspondence alignment proposed), and what the rerun on the same proof cache took from the first run:

| Part | Kind | Verdict | On the rerun | Why not verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /quotes` | entry point | refuted | an exact hit |  |
| `POST /quotes/text` | entry point | unresolved | not a proof | `what the analysis can't see stays unresolved: the old build: a dynamic call site the walk doesn't follow: StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants in QuotesController.quoteText(long, int) (string concatenation: the string's value isn't modeled); the new build: a dynamic call site the walk doesn't follow: StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants in QuotesController.quoteText(long, int) (string concatenation: the string's value isn't modeled)` |
| `shop.Pricing#discount` | kernel | verified | an exact hit |  |
| `shop.Pricing#total` | kernel | verified | an exact hit; `Pricing.discount` proved on its own and taken as one function |  |
| `shop.Pricing#withQuantity` | kernel | verified | an exact hit |  |
| `shop.Money#cents (was shop.Quote#cents)` | kernel | unresolved | not a proof | `class not found in the previous version: shop.Money` |
| `shop.Quote#quantity` | kernel | unresolved | not a proof | `the receiver is made differently in the two versions: this: a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(cents: long, quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts before, this: a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(amount: Money(cents: long), quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts now; a receiver of another construction or other fields is not supported yet` |

Obligations, one per observation of an old entry point: 7 preserved, 1 unresolved. Decisions a person made, by category: approved exclusion 0, domain restriction 0, environment assumption 0, mapping 0, observation change 0.

No question is left for a person.

What the verdicts rest on that nobody decided (assumed, not approved):

- KafkaTemplate.send is a recording stub in both builds: a recorded attempt is the call attempted, with its payload snapshotted at the call, not a delivery or a commit
- every modeled call returns normally, the environment model's only outcome: a failure of a store, broker or client is outside the claim
- QuotesController is made by its constructor with every dependency null and every other argument zero, in both builds: its dependencies are reached only through the modeled calls, and configuration it would be given is the type's default
- a payload string is snapshotted as the literal it is, among those of either build; any other string leaves the result unresolved
- at most 4 attempts are recorded, exactly in order; one more leaves the result unresolved

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

No: every existing unit test passes (`java -ea shop.Tests`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

A rewrite of the glue around a kernel can lose a send for a case nobody tests, and nothing the route returns shows it: the consumer of the `quotes` topic just never hears of the order.

## Why the verdict is right

The route's observation spec makes each `KafkaTemplate.send` an observation, with the payload paths a consumer reads (`data.total`, `data.quantity`) snapshotted at the call. Both builds' sends are replaced by the same recording stub, and the tool's own checker proves or refutes that the two logs are equal, in exact order. On a quote of 100 items with a positive total, the old build attempts one send and the new one none.

## What to do

Send the event for every positive total, as before.

## Notes

- Checked by `jvmcontract compare`, which build.py runs as the B9 check of the shop app (`run_tool_compare`): the unpatched build against the patched one, twice under one fresh proof cache, the verdict read from the rerun and the page's output from the first run. The verdict is the subject's; the page lists every other part the run checked.
- The joint example of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md`'s Phase 5, made an example: the app's sources are the fixture's `before` build (`lib/tests/fixtures/foundations/`), and the patch turns them into its `after` build with the dropped-effect defect (`defects/dropped-effect/`) overlaid. `lib/tests/compare.rs` holds `jvmcontract compare` to the same builds inline; this is the same run by build.py, with the app's tests run too.
- Nothing in the run is written by hand. The entry points' external inputs (`cents`, `quantity`) are anchored by their observation specs, so no mapping is involved at the boundary. The kernel's relation between the old and new quotes (`old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents`, `old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity`) is alignment's proposal, inferred from how the two constructors route their parameters into the fields; it stays *proposed*, its evidence the proof under its claim key, and since nothing external anchors a kernel method's inputs, a proved relation there is reported as proved and not as the intended one.
- What stays unresolved in every example of the set, by name: `POST /quotes/text` (its string concatenation isn't modeled), `Quote#cents` moved to `Money#cents` (a method of a class the old build doesn't have) and `Quote#quantity`, whose receiver is made differently in the two versions (`Quote(long, int)` before, `Quote(Money, int)` now), which the regression check doesn't relate yet. Before the application-core merge (2026-11-08) it was refused as an instance method instead; the merge's check takes a receiver made by its constructor, of the same construction in both versions.
- Run inline on 2026-11-07 (JDK 25.0.5), `jvmcontract compare` on the app compiled unpatched and patched, as build.py compiles it, and on the fixture's builds, with the same verdicts (the times are the fixture's): `POST /quotes` refuted, replayed on a JVM under the recording stubs; the kernel's `total`, `withQuantity` and `discount` verified. 0.4 s cold, 0.2 s warm.
- The app's tests pass on this version: none sends 100 items.
